title: Female borrowers who mention higher loan amounts in their pitch text may fund more slowly.
For male borrowers, using the loan for business inventory may be faster than using it for education.
Female borrowers who mention specific personal or household deficits fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention having previous loans may fund faster.
The use of the phrase 'hardworking entrepreneur' in female pitches may predict faster funding.
Mentioning a general store business may accelerate funding for female borrowers.
Female borrowers who specify the number of children may fund faster.
Mentioning previous loan history or a credit record may accelerate funding for female borrowers.
Female borrowers who explicitly describe their skills or character traits may fund faster.
Pitches from women that include the borrower's age tend to fund more slowly than those that omit it.
Mentioning specific institutional or brand names predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Explicit expressions of gratitude to lenders accelerate funding for female borrowers.
Specifying the number of years the business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention benefits to their family or community fund faster.
Mentioning benefits for children predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Mentioning home or living condition improvements accelerates funding for women but slows it for men.
Female borrowers who mention the loan amount in local currency fund more slowly.
